names.legendary: Queen Honeycombe the Industrious

lore.common: Bumps into the same window forty times, then flies straight out of the open door beside it.
lore.uncommon: Comes home so covered in pollen that it looks like a tiny flying cheese puff.
lore.rare: Does a wiggly dance that tells the whole hive exactly where your picnic jam is.
lore.epic: Swarmed into the bakery and tasted every doughnut through the glass. The baker now sells them as pre-licked.
lore.legendary: Danced the waggle dance so well that the whole hive flew to the ice-cream van instead of the clover. The van now has a queue of very sticky customers.

names.legendary: Scarabella, Roller of the Desert

lore.common: Falls on its back and waves its legs in the air until someone helps it, then walks off without thanks.
lore.uncommon: Rolls a ball of dung bigger than itself across the field and won't let anyone help.
lore.rare: Its shell shines so brightly in the sun that magpies keep trying to steal it.
lore.epic: Marched a rhinoceros-beetle army under the patio and lifted every paving stone half a centimetre. The garden table now wobbles on purpose.
lore.legendary: Steered by the stars to roll its ball across the entire desert in a perfectly straight line, then started a second one.

names.legendary: Armadillo Prime, Keeper of the Logs

lore.common: Rolls into a ball when someone lifts its flowerpot, then refuses to come out for interviews.
lore.uncommon: Has fourteen legs and still loses every race against a snail.
lore.rare: Drinks up all the dampness in the cellar and turns the floorboards into a perfect little desert.
lore.epic: Gathered ten thousand woodlice beneath a log and marched it across the garden. The gardener declared it an unidentified vehicle.
lore.legendary: The oldest Isopod carries a tiny forest on its armour. Every fallen leaf feeds another creature, and not even winter can empty its kingdom beneath the logs.

names.legendary: Chrysovela, Mother of the Golden Lace

lore.common: Settles on the bedroom lamp like a delicate green ghost with terrible timing.
lore.uncommon: Wears wings of such fine lace that a spider once asked where it shops.
lore.rare: Can clear an entire rosebush of aphids before breakfast. The roses send thank-you cards.
lore.epic: Raised a battalion of hungry larvae to defend a blighted orchard. By spring the leaves gleamed untouched, and the aphids had founded a complaints department.
lore.legendary: Chrysovela hangs her eggs from threads thinner than moonlight. When the orchards are threatened, the little lanterns hatch into a silent green army no pest can outrun.

names.legendary: Chrysomelda, the Emerald Hunger

lore.common: Eats a little hole in each lettuce leaf so the salad looks like it has lace trim.
lore.uncommon: Polishes its glittering shell while munching the gardener's favourite plant.
lore.rare: Drops from a leaf and plays dead so convincingly that the gardener holds a tiny funeral.
lore.epic: Invaded the allotment in sparkling ranks and turned every cabbage into a fashionable lace fan. The gardeners are still refusing to call it art.
lore.legendary: Chrysomelda once ate the royal garden's greatest rose without leaving its shape behind. Only the perfect portrait of the queen cut into the remaining leaf revealed where the flower had gone.

names.legendary: Cicadella, Jumper of the Sunlit Veins

lore.common: Leaps off its leaf the instant someone tries to photograph it, usually onto their nose.
lore.uncommon: Sidesteps round a stem like a tiny secret agent avoiding eye contact.
lore.rare: Sends songs through plant veins, turning the whole tomato patch into a humming choir.
lore.epic: Summoned a thousand tiny jumpers that bounced through the greenhouse like green popcorn. The windows rang like bells with every landing.
lore.legendary: Cicadella once leapt from the highest branch to catch a falling seed before it touched earth. The seed took root in mid-air, and a floating garden still blooms above the orchard.

names.legendary: Cerambyx, the Forest's Living Compass

lore.common: Walks into doors because its antennae arrive before it does.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks like an old cupboard hinge when lifted, then acts as though it was intentional.
lore.rare: Carves secret tunnels through dead wood and leaves its own initials in the sawdust.
lore.epic: Raised its antennae above the pines and caught an entire storm between them. The forest listened to thunder played like a violin.
lore.legendary: Cerambyx's horns have mapped every tree ever felled in the ancient woodland. At its call, their roots awaken beneath the soil and reach for the sun again.

names.legendary: Mantissa, the Thousand-Second Strike

lore.common: Folds its arms politely while quietly deciding which fly to eat for lunch.
lore.uncommon: Turns its head to stare behind itself with the judgement of a suspicious school librarian.
lore.rare: Waits perfectly still on a flower until an insect chooses its arm as a resting place.
lore.epic: Won the garden tournament without taking a single step, defeating every challenger with one lightning-fast grasp.
lore.legendary: Mantissa waited through a hundred rainy seasons for a single perfect strike. When her folded blades finally opened, the falling rain seemed to pause in respect.

names.legendary: Cicindrake, the Hunter Who Outran Sight

lore.common: Sprints after an ant, overshoots it by a metre and pretends it was sightseeing.
lore.uncommon: Wears a metallic emerald shell and insists every race needs a victory photograph.
lore.rare: Runs so fast its eyes lose focus, so it freezes to hunt by memory and strikes before prey can blink.
lore.epic: Raced across a desert at such speed that its own dust devil became a second, much slower beetle and demanded a rematch.
lore.legendary: Cicindrake once chased a falling star across the salt flats and caught its reflection before the star landed. Its jaws still sparkle with borrowed starlight.

names.legendary: Trilovox, the Memory in the Stone

lore.common: Scuttles across the seabed and looks shocked that nobody recognises its ancient face.
lore.uncommon: Rolls into a bumpy ball and pretends it is a particularly interesting pebble.
lore.rare: Wakes from fossil sleep to correct museum labels and leaves the geologists deeply unsettled.
lore.epic: Emerged with a thousand long-forgotten companions from a cliff face and marched into the sea like an armoured parade from prehistory.
lore.legendary: Trilovox survived the ages by sealing one whisper of the ancient ocean inside its shell. When a curious child lifted the fossil to her ear, the forgotten sea whispered her name.

names.legendary: Monarcha, Queen of the Long Migration

lore.common: Lands on your nose, poses for a photo, then leaves before the camera opens.
lore.uncommon: Paints elaborate patterns on its wings, then spends the day telling flowers they copied it.
lore.rare: Tastes ancient secrets through its feet. Mostly discovers that the garden path is filthy.
lore.epic: Summoned a cloud of wings so vast the valley turned into moving stained glass. Every window demanded an apology for being outclassed.
lore.legendary: Guides fragile wings across oceans and centuries to the trees their ancestors knew. Even hurricanes part for her procession, though she still gets lost in supermarkets.

names.legendary: Lycaena, the Butterfly With Two Faces

lore.common: Looks like a scrap of blue sky that forgot how to stay up.
lore.uncommon: Sends its caterpillars to dine with ants and never returns their borrowed sugar.
lore.rare: Tricks hungry birds into striking its false head while the real one slips away.
lore.epic: Covered the entire meadow in blue wings until passing clouds tried to land among them. The farmer charged admission to the sky.
lore.legendary: Lycaena fooled the hunters of a thousand summers with the false eyes on its wings. Legends say it wears the final blue of every vanished flower.

names.legendary: Lunamoth, Bride of the Borrowed Moon

lore.common: Bumps the same bulb for hours, convinced this time it will finally open the door.
lore.uncommon: Leaves lacework holes in a wool jumper and considers itself a fashion designer.
lore.rare: Scatters wing dust that reveals the shapes of things hidden in darkness. Usually crumbs.
lore.epic: Ate through the costume department before opening night. The actors performed an entire royal tragedy wearing extremely fashionable holes.
lore.legendary: Lunamoth followed a false moon made of lantern glass until dawn. The real Moon, moved by such devotion, now leaves one silver thread on its wings each night.

names.legendary: Aphantara, Watcher of the Twilight Grass

lore.common: Flutters through the grass like a brown leaf that forgot how to fall.
lore.uncommon: Hides its little eye-spots until a curious bird gets far too close.
lore.rare: Flies through rain and cloud when every other butterfly stays home.
lore.epic: Filled the meadow with a thousand eye-spotted wings, making the entire field appear to blink at once.
lore.legendary: Aphantara brought every butterfly of the valley to a twilight ball. Their eye-spotted wings made the constellations blink in embarrassment.

names.legendary: Phoebelle, Herald of the First Gold

lore.common: Puddles in the mud and insists yellow wings are suitable formalwear.
lore.uncommon: Flutters past a lemon tree and makes the fruit jealous of its colouring.
lore.rare: Flashes across fields so quickly that the birds see only floating drops of sunshine.
lore.epic: Gathered a golden cloud of butterflies over the annual fair and turned the entire merry-go-round into a revolving sunset.
lore.legendary: Phoebelle carried the first yellow of spring through a world of endless grey. Each wingbeat restored colour to one flower, until the hills bloomed behind her.

names.legendary: Metamorphax, Devourer of Its Former Self

lore.common: Eats holes in every leaf and sleeps on the evidence. An excellent criminal.
lore.uncommon: Moves by folding itself like an accordion. The garden snails consider this showing off.
lore.rare: Inflates fake serpent eyes on its back to terrify hungry birds. It is absolutely delighted when it works.
lore.epic: Spun a cocoon so enormous that the greenhouse vanished beneath silk. A week later something with six thousand wings asked where the door was.
lore.legendary: Metamorphax remembers every life it has lived, from crawling grub to monarch of the skies. Its greatest terror is becoming ordinary again, so it keeps evolving.

names.legendary: Centorax, Emperor of the Endless March

lore.common: Runs out from under the bathroom mat and makes everyone reconsider owning a bathroom.
lore.uncommon: Has so many legs that putting on socks is a full-time job. It refuses to do unpaid overtime.
lore.rare: Can outrun its own shadow around the skirting board. The shadow filed for transfer.
lore.epic: Marched through a mansion with an army of a million tiny legs. By morning every slipper had migrated to the attic.
lore.legendary: Centorax counts its footsteps instead of sheep when it cannot sleep. Legends say the counting once lasted a thousand years and the ground began to march with it.

names.legendary: Lumbragon, Architect of the Living Earth

lore.common: Emerges after rain and looks offended that the pavement is still hard.
lore.uncommon: Eats soil like a gourmet and gives every flowerbed a detailed restaurant review.
lore.rare: Can tunnel beneath a stone wall overnight. The mole considers this cheating.
lore.epic: Led a million worms through a barren field and turned it into a lush garden by sunrise. The farmer offered them a tractor; they declined.
lore.legendary: In the age before ploughs, Lumbragon carved the paths through which roots learned to breathe. Every living forest rests upon its patient, winding work.

names.legendary: Hirudelle, the Unforgotten Attachment

lore.common: Grabs an ankle in the pond and acts hurt when asked to let go.
lore.uncommon: Stretches like a rubber band across the muddy bottom, taking its time to get anywhere.
lore.rare: Sneaks home on a fisherman's boot and declares the garden pond its second residence.
lore.epic: Stretched across a stream and convinced every duckling it was a bridge. The parents are still leaving it bread as a toll.
lore.legendary: Hirudelle once attached itself to the boots of a wandering giant and travelled the world without taking a step. It now knows every river by taste and every traveller by the stories they leave.

names.legendary: Millipedia, the Patient Queen of Soil

lore.common: Curls into a perfect spiral whenever a curious child lifts its flowerpot.
lore.uncommon: Walks with so many rippling legs that the garden path seems to be moving.
lore.rare: Releases a peculiar defensive scent when frightened. Even the robin decides it has a better appointment elsewhere.
lore.epic: Led a thousand cousins on a midnight parade through the greenhouse. Every flowerpot woke up two steps closer to the door.
lore.legendary: Millipedia has walked beneath the forest floor since the oldest trees were seedlings. Each of her countless footsteps turns fallen leaves into the soil of tomorrow.

names.legendary: Homarok, the Unbreakable Tideking

lore.common: Has one claw for cracking shells and another for shaking hands. Both are terrible at shaking hands.
lore.uncommon: Sheds its armour when it grows. Leaves the empty shell sitting at the dinner table to frighten the cook.
lore.rare: Escaped a seafood tank by clicking its claws in the rhythm of the security keypad. The owner now uses facial recognition.
lore.epic: Emerged from the harbour wearing an entire shipwreck as armour. It demanded tribute in mussels and accidentally became the new harbourmaster.
lore.legendary: Homarok's ancient claws can close the jaws of a storm. Fishermen still leave a single mussel on the pier each year, hoping the Tideking remembers their generosity.

names.legendary: Carcinox, Emperor of the Sideways Seas

lore.common: Pinches your toe, then scuttles away as if you started it.
lore.uncommon: Builds a tiny sandcastle, declares itself king and evicts the seagulls.
lore.rare: Commands rockpool armies by waving one enormous claw. Its soldiers mostly argue over shells.
lore.epic: Led a sideways invasion of the beach, rearranging every sandcastle into an exact likeness of its own face.
lore.legendary: Carcinox once walked across the ocean floor without taking a single forward step. When offered the crown of the sea, it demanded the throne be installed sideways.

names.legendary: Uca, the One-Clawed Conductor

lore.common: Waves its giant claw like a tourist trying to hail a taxi.
lore.uncommon: Can turn a mudflat into a dance floor using just one oversized pincer.
lore.rare: Conducts a hundred neighbouring crabs by waving its claw. The seagulls are not invited.
lore.epic: Orchestrated a thousand-claw performance at low tide. The surf kept rhythm, and the lighthouse flashed an encore all night.
lore.legendary: Uca challenged the moon to a duel for command of the tides. Every time the ocean recedes, the great fiddler raises its single claw and claims another victory.

names.legendary: Pagurian, the Wandering Palace

lore.common: Inspects every empty shell on the beach, then complains about the lack of cupboards.
lore.uncommon: Forms a queue with its friends to exchange homes. Nobody likes the middle-sized shell.
lore.rare: Moves into a bottle cap and decorates it with pebbles, declaring it a luxury apartment.
lore.epic: Occupied a lost fisherman's boot and marched it down the beach like a warship. The gulls asked for passports.
lore.legendary: Pagurian has worn a thousand shells across a thousand shores. The oldest is a spiral palace that appears only at low tide and has room for every homeless crab.

names.legendary: Odonarion, Sword of the Summer Sky

lore.common: Hovers outside windows to supervise everybody's lunch.
lore.uncommon: Can fly backwards faster than some insects fly forward. Mentions it constantly.
lore.rare: Hunts mosquitoes with such precision that the entire pond now calls it Sir.
lore.epic: Its four wings stirred a spiral of wind above the marsh, sweeping every mosquito into a distant cloud. The campers declared a holiday.
lore.legendary: Before birds conquered the sky, Odonarion patrolled it on wings of living glass. Even the ancient storms learned to make room for its flight.

names.legendary: Polymor, the Thousandth Transformation

lore.common: Has a tail twice as long as its attention span.
lore.uncommon: Grows two tiny legs and spends the afternoon showing them to the ducklings.
lore.rare: Can swap between tadpole and frog at will, much to the bewilderment of the heron.
lore.epic: Summoned ten thousand siblings from the pond, turning a garden puddle into a hopping amphibian army overnight.
lore.legendary: Polymor remembers every form ever taken beneath the water: egg, tail, legs and leap. Once each spring it returns to the pond to teach the youngest the courage to change.

names.legendary: Sir Croakalot, the Prince in Waiting

lore.common: Jumps into the pond with a huge splash right next to anyone who's just sat down.
lore.uncommon: Croaks so loudly on summer nights that the neighbours have bought earplugs.
lore.rare: Flicks its tongue out so fast that it catches flies before they've even noticed it.
lore.epic: Jumped into the garden pond so hard that every goldfish ended up in the birdbath.
lore.legendary: Was kissed by a hundred hopeful princesses and stayed a frog every time. Says it's quite happy, thank you.

names.legendary: Ascaphor, the Wordless Torrent

lore.common: Sticks to river stones so firmly that even the current gives up arguing.
lore.uncommon: Cannot croak, so sends important messages by waving one damp little foot.
lore.rare: Clings upside down beneath a waterfall where the trout refuse to swim.
lore.epic: Climbed a cascading mountain river against its own torrent, guiding stranded froglets through every roaring rapid.
lore.legendary: Ascaphor guards the one spring where the mountain never stops singing. Silent among the waterfalls, it hears the smallest heartbeat carried downstream.

names.legendary: Croakmord, Baron of the Crooked Pond

lore.common: Blocks the garden path and looks offended when asked to move.
lore.uncommon: Sheds its skin, eats it and insists nobody witnessed its disgusting table manners.
lore.rare: Clears an entire vegetable patch of slugs, then demands the largest flowerpot as payment.
lore.epic: Croaked so powerfully that every garden gnome in the county marched into the marsh to attend its emergency council.
lore.legendary: Croakmord has sat beneath the same mossy stone for five hundred rainy seasons. Every lost traveller in the bog hears one grumpy croak pointing them safely home.

names.legendary: Coccinella, the Sevenfold Blessing

lore.common: Marches to the end of your finger and forgets what flying is for.
lore.uncommon: Insists its spots be counted before every take-off. Miscounting is unacceptable.
lore.rare: Devours a rosebush's aphids overnight and leaves one polite thank-you note for the gardener.
lore.epic: Gathered a thousand red-winged guardians above the dying orchard. Their arrival covered the trees like scarlet blossoms and sent every pest running.
lore.legendary: Coccinella carries seven spots said to be blessings from the first spring. Every garden it visits remembers how to bloom, even after a winter that should have lasted forever.

names.legendary: Chromael, Keeper of the Unseen Sun

lore.common: Keeps one eye on dinner and the other on tomorrow. Tomorrow looks suspicious.
lore.uncommon: Sways like a leaf to avoid being seen. Once fooled a tree into adopting it.
lore.rare: Changes colour with its moods. A particularly offended shade of purple has been outlawed in three palaces.
lore.epic: Disguised itself as a rainbow so convincingly that the sky copied it. The valley endured three days of multicoloured rain.
lore.legendary: Chromael once stole every colour from the sunrise. The kingdom lived in black and white until someone complimented its scales.

names.legendary: Sobekar, the River That Bites

lore.common: Pretends to be a log until somebody sits down for a picnic. Then the log asks for a sandwich.
lore.uncommon: Only its eyes rise above the river. It has been judging passing boats for years.
lore.rare: Its grin can frighten a whole riverbank into silence. The little birds cleaning its teeth remain unimpressed.
lore.epic: Blocked the Nile with a single enormous yawn. Three villages paid in fish to persuade it to close its mouth.
lore.legendary: The river changes course whenever Sobekar turns in his sleep. Cartographers call it erosion; priests call it a crocodile.

names.legendary: Agamagon, Emperor of a Thousand Suns

lore.common: Performs push-ups on hot rocks to impress absolutely anyone. Even the rocks are getting tired of it.
lore.uncommon: Its orange head and blue body make it look like two lizards arguing over a costume.
lore.rare: Nods with such authority that other lizards start following orders nobody actually gave.
lore.epic: Nodded at a mountain until the mountain nodded back. The resulting tremor was registered as a very enthusiastic greeting.
lore.legendary: Every push-up lifts the sun one finger-width higher. The last time Agamagon reached a hundred, winter lodged a formal complaint.

names.legendary: Gerrhonax, Serpent of the Turning Wheel

lore.common: Leaves its tail behind when startled. The tail is considerably braver than the rest of it.
lore.uncommon: Unfolds its loose side scales after lunch and insists it has not gained any weight.
lore.rare: Hides inside gardening gloves and whispers "surprise" with its tiny scaly face. The gardener is considering a new career.
lore.epic: Slid beneath a greenhouse so swiftly that the ground rippled like a wave. Every slug packed its bags that afternoon.
lore.legendary: Curled into a living wheel and outran the thunder across seven hills. Ancient cartmakers copied its trick and called it progress.

names.legendary: Gatorax, Emperor of the Blackwater

lore.common: Pretends to be a log until a golf ball lands nearby. Then it becomes a very expensive log.
lore.uncommon: Bellows so deeply that the pond gets ripples in places where there is no water. The frogs file noise complaints.
lore.rare: Carves secret pools into the marsh with its tail. Charges visiting turtles one compliment per night.
lore.epic: Rose from the bayou and dragged an entire riverboat upstream by its anchor. The passengers left five stars for the unusually scenic tour.
lore.legendary: Gatorax has ruled the blackwater since before the first river found its course. Its scales bear the names of vanished swamps, and it still refuses to return a single golf ball.

names.legendary: Anolisk, the Emerald Pretender

lore.common: Puffs up a pink throat fan whenever it feels brave. It feels brave around flies and very small leaves.
lore.uncommon: Changes from green to brown when embarrassed. Has been brown ever since it fell off the porch railing.
lore.rare: Flicks its glowing throat fan and makes its rivals forget what they were arguing about. Usually it was a fence.
lore.epic: Declared a porch railing its kingdom and summoned a battalion of tiny anoles. The homeowner now needs a royal permit to hang washing.
lore.legendary: Anolisk can cloak an entire palace in the colours of the surrounding forest. Kings have sought its protection for centuries; it insists on being paid in sun-warmed bricks.

names.legendary: Coleonyx, the Moonstripe Phantom

lore.common: Chirps from behind a rock the moment you are trying to sleep. Denies being there.
lore.uncommon: Waves its striped tail like a tiny angry cat before pouncing on something smaller than a raisin.
lore.rare: Walks on tiptoe across moonlit sand and steals crickets straight out of their songs.
lore.epic: Turned an entire desert campsite silent in a single night. The tourists applauded; the crickets filed a complaint.
lore.legendary: An elusive striped guardian that hunts by moonlight and vanishes at dawn. Its footprints can be seen only when the stars are reflected in them.

names.legendary: Triturion, Keeper of the Hidden Spring

lore.common: Hides beneath a flowerpot for winter and treats every gardener as an intruder.
lore.uncommon: Grows a fancy crest in spring and makes the frogs feel underdressed.
lore.rare: Flashes its orange belly so brightly that the heron thinks sunset has arrived at noon and flies home for bed.
lore.epic: Called a hundred newts from the garden ponds and flooded the greenhouse with tiny web-footed sorcerers. The watering cans surrendered.
lore.legendary: Triturion knows a secret pond that appears only beneath the first spring moon. Its waters can heal a wounded forest, though the newts demand absolute silence during spawning season.

names.legendary: Notophyr, Keeper of the Orange Road

lore.common: Is bright orange and still somehow gets lost in a pile of autumn leaves.
lore.uncommon: Goes exploring on rainy days, then complains that the forest is damp.
lore.rare: Its glowing skin warns hungry birds to stay away. The robins claim they cannot read the sign.
lore.epic: Led a procession of fire-colored newts through the woodland after a storm. The hikers mistook them for a river of fallen autumn leaves.
lore.legendary: Notophyr walked the forest floor for a thousand seasons before choosing a pond. It remembers every path the trees ever made, including those buried beneath new roots.

names.legendary: Salamandra, Keeper of the False Flame

lore.common: Wears bright yellow warning signs all over its back. Nobody can read the small print.
lore.uncommon: Lives beneath a damp log and claims the forest path is its private driveway.
lore.rare: Its bitter skin has discouraged every fox in the woods. One now eats only toast.
lore.epic: Crawled out of a cold hearth during a thunderstorm and convinced the village it had been born in fire. The local dragon resigned in embarrassment.
lore.legendary: For centuries Salamandra was blamed for every flame that survived a storm. The truth is stranger: it kept the ancient hearth dry by sleeping beneath its stones.

names.legendary: Lord Ruffas, the Walking Sunburst

lore.common: Opens its huge neck frill whenever someone steps near, like an umbrella opening in your face.
lore.uncommon: Raises its neck frill to frighten a butterfly. The butterfly asks if it has a spare umbrella.
lore.rare: Can sprint on two legs while shouting like an offended kettle. Even the dingo pretends not to notice.
lore.epic: Opened its enormous frill in the middle of the outback highway. An entire road train reversed because the driver thought the desert had grown teeth.
lore.legendary: Legends tell of Lord Ruffas, whose colossal frill eclipsed the noon sun. The people worshipped the new moon until he sneezed and folded it away.

names.legendary: Helodrake, the Sun-Baked Tyrant

lore.common: Bites onto things and won't let go, including the doormat.
lore.uncommon: Stores enough food in its tail to survive a whole season of naps. Has never been happier.
lore.rare: Walks so slowly that the lizards behind it start forming a queue.
lore.epic: Held its ground against a pack of coyotes with one long hiss. They now take the scenic route.
lore.legendary: Helodrake sleeps beneath a sun-baked mesa with venom strong enough to quiet a desert storm. When it wakes, the rocks themselves creep away to give it room.

names.legendary: Lazuli, the Azure-Throated Regent

lore.common: Basks on the wall until the back door squeaks, then vanishes faster than gossip.
lore.uncommon: Turns its back a spectacular green so the grass believes it has another leaf.
lore.rare: Outsprints a chasing cat across three garden walls without spilling the beetle in its mouth.
lore.epic: Declared every sunny stone in the village part of its territory. The cats have been issued visitor permits.
lore.legendary: Every spring Lazuli's throat turns blue as a tiny summer sky. Legends say the first warm day begins only when it raises its head to sing.

names.legendary: Ignatius, Keeper of the Warmest Rock

lore.common: Claims the best stone at sunrise and charges the beetles admission.
lore.uncommon: Leaves a twitching tail behind to distract the cat, then sneaks back to steal the cat's food.
lore.rare: Runs up a sheer garden wall and taps on the bedroom window to ask why everyone is still asleep.
lore.epic: Summoned a thousand sunbathing lizards onto the castle ramparts. The guards surrendered their warm helmets by noon.
lore.legendary: Ignatius once caught the dying sunset in his scales and held its warmth through a century of winters. Every cold-blooded creature knows the way to his rock.

names.legendary: Ambystra, Guardian of the Hidden Pool

lore.common: Emerges from beneath a log only when the weather forecast says 'absolutely miserable'.
lore.uncommon: Counts its yellow spots at night and invents new ones when it gets bored.
lore.rare: Knows the secret paths to every woodland breeding pool, even those lost beneath centuries of fallen leaves.
lore.epic: Led the spotted salamanders across a busy highway in one silent midnight procession. Every traffic light turned green for the wrong direction.
lore.legendary: Ambystra carries the memory of every spring rain in her yellow spots. When the last forest pond dried, she opened one spot and filled it again.

names.legendary: Aspidessa, Daughter of the Sunlit Sands

lore.common: Stops halfway across the trail to look smug, then vanishes into the dust.
lore.uncommon: Zigzags over hot stones so quickly its own tail gets dizzy.
lore.rare: Races between cactus shadows without ever leaving a footprint.
lore.epic: Led a glittering procession of desert lizards through a sandstorm, opening a winding path for lost hikers to follow.
lore.legendary: Survived the harshest summers without a single companion to guide her. From her tracks sprang a whole line of swift daughters, each as fearless as the first.

names.legendary: Octaplate, Sentinel of the Endless Shore

lore.common: Hugs one rock so tightly that the tide has begun calling it furniture.
lore.uncommon: Wears eight armour plates and polishes all of them with a seaweed toothbrush.
lore.rare: Scrapes algae from stone using teeth tougher than iron. The dentist has asked it to stop showing off.
lore.epic: Anchored itself to the reef during a storm so violent that the entire island drifted while its rock stayed put.
lore.legendary: Octaplate has clung to the first rock ever lifted from the ocean. Eight ancient plates bear eight forgotten seas, and no wave has ever persuaded it to move.

names.legendary: Planaria, the Thousandfold Survivor

lore.common: Slides along the aquarium glass like a forgotten ribbon from a birthday present.
lore.uncommon: Can make a new friend by splitting in two. Its birthdays are very complicated.
lore.rare: Grows back whatever it loses, including an entire head with an equally bad sense of direction.
lore.epic: Split into a hundred copies during the laboratory school visit. By lunch, every science teacher had acquired an identical assistant asking for biscuits.
lore.legendary: Planaria has survived the rise and fall of empires by endlessly renewing itself. It remembers every ruler it ever met, and judges them chiefly on the quality of their ponds.

names.legendary: Nematara, Queen of the Unseen

lore.common: Wiggles through a spoonful of soil with a million companions and never remembers anybody's name.
lore.uncommon: Draws a winding S-shape beneath the vegetable patch, as if practising its signature.
lore.rare: Ties the roots of tomato plants into tiny knots. The gardener thinks the plants are trying to knit.
lore.epic: Called its countless cousins from beneath the fields and made the earth ripple like a sleeping creature waking. The potatoes grew faces of absolute astonishment.
lore.legendary: Nematara commands armies too small for human eyes, dwelling from the highest peaks to the ocean floor. When the great beasts vanished, her hidden kingdom remained.

names.legendary: Holothuria, Gardener of the Ocean Floor

lore.common: Looks like a lost sausage on the seabed and insists this is camouflage.
lore.uncommon: Eats sand for breakfast and leaves neatly swept paths behind it, to the delight of tiny crabs.
lore.rare: Fires a sticky tangle of threads at a nosy predator, then slips away looking completely innocent.
lore.epic: Filtered an entire bay's seabed in a single afternoon. The tourists arrived to find the water crystal clear and the sea cucumber asking for a holiday.
lore.legendary: Holothuria can restore what she has lost, even after the sea takes almost everything. Once she regrew herself beside a sunken ship and became its last living gardener.

names.legendary: Nudibrancha, Living Jewel of the Reef

lore.common: Dresses in colours so bright that the clownfish ask for fashion advice.
lore.uncommon: Wears feathery gills like a ridiculous ceremonial hat and is very pleased with the effect.
lore.rare: Eats a stinging sea creature and borrows its defence. The original owner would like it back.
lore.epic: Painted the entire reef with the colours of a hundred glowing sea slugs. The visiting divers forgot about their treasure hunt.
lore.legendary: Nudibrancha carries stolen lightning from sea anemones in the folds of her frilled skin. The currents part around her like courtiers around a queen.

names.legendary: Limaxara, the Crownless Queen of Slime

lore.common: Leaves a glittering trail straight across the newly cleaned patio and looks terribly pleased.
lore.uncommon: Eats only the prize-winning lettuce, ignoring the weeds as a matter of principle.
lore.rare: Slips through a locked door's keyhole and raids a vegetable patch without leaving a single footprint.
lore.epic: Led a midnight army of slugs across the allotments. By dawn every cabbage wore an expensive-looking lace collar of holes.
lore.legendary: Limaxara once slid across a kingdom without raising a sound, leaving a silver road for the lost to follow home. Her greatest enemy remains a bowl of salt and a very determined gardener.

names.legendary: Escargoth, the Wanderer Who Carried Dawn

lore.common: Climbs the garden wall and refuses to come down until the rain starts.
lore.uncommon: Occupies a lettuce leaf like a luxurious apartment and eats the rent.
lore.rare: Leaves a silver trail that guides lost insects home through the dark garden.
lore.epic: Challenged the entire racing club to a marathon and arrived a month late with a medal it had made itself.
lore.legendary: Escargoth carried a tiny sunrise in his spiral shell across the longest night. When he finally reached the far garden wall, every flower opened and the birds politely let him sleep in.

names.legendary: Crotalith, Oracle of the Desert Rattle

lore.common: Shakes its tail at tumbleweeds, stones and suspicious-looking hats.
lore.uncommon: Wears a diamond pattern more fashionable than the cowboy who spotted it.
lore.rare: Counts approaching footsteps in the vibrations of the earth, then sends a loud warning to turn back.
lore.epic: Its rattle echoed across the canyon until the rocks themselves shook in rhythm. Even the tumbleweeds stopped to listen.
lore.legendary: Every ring on Crotalith's ancient rattle marks a desert season survived. Wanderers say its warning can reveal the only safe route through a sandstorm.

names.legendary: Thamnoria, Keeper of the Garden Paths

lore.common: Slithers out of the compost to supervise gardening. Has opinions about how the spade is being used.
lore.uncommon: Has a striped coat that looks like a tiny referee's uniform. Blows no whistle but judges everyone.
lore.rare: Can release an awful smell at will. It has never lost an argument with a lawnmower.
lore.epic: Wove through a thousand garden hoses at a summer fair and convinced the entire town the hoses were alive.
lore.legendary: Thamnoria is the ancient serpent beneath the allotments, guarding the roots of the first tree. Gardeners leave her eggs and never ask which kind she prefers.

names.legendary: Dendralisk, the Unseen Emerald

lore.common: Hides in a tree so well that a parrot once tried to hang its nest from it.
lore.uncommon: Slides through bright leaves like a green ribbon fleeing a present.
lore.rare: Crosses an entire canopy in one blink. The monkey watching it drops three bananas in astonishment.
lore.epic: Shot between the crowns of a thousand jungle trees before a single falling leaf could touch the ground. The forest called it green lightning.
lore.legendary: Dendralisk guarded a hidden treetop garden for generations. Intruders saw only moving leaves, while the elders knew every rustle was a warning.

names.legendary: Ophelia, the Ribbon in the Reeds

lore.common: Pretends to be a blade of grass until someone tries to tie their shoelaces beside it.
lore.uncommon: Hangs from a vine so patiently that a butterfly mistakes it for a very thin branch.
lore.rare: Can catch a cricket without disturbing a single grass stem. Its neighbours call it the silent picnic thief.
lore.epic: Wove through the entire meadow at dusk, leaving a perfect maze of swaying grass. The sheep followed the wrong paths home.
lore.legendary: Ophelia hides in the meadow's oldest reeds and guards its quiet music. Each night she catches the noisiest cricket so the others may finish their songs.

names.legendary: Heterodon, Master of the Last Curtain

lore.common: Rolls onto its back and sticks out its tongue whenever somebody looks at it sternly.
lore.uncommon: Digs through soft soil with its upturned nose, sending tiny showers of sand onto passing beetles.
lore.rare: Puffs itself into a terrifying cobra shape, then remembers it is supposed to be lying down playing dead.
lore.epic: Performed such a convincing death scene in the village garden that even the funeral director arrived with flowers. It accepted the bouquet.
lore.legendary: Heterodon fooled the first desert hawk by playing dead for three days. Every predator since has had to sit through the entire performance, including a very dramatic curtain call.

names.legendary: Cerastor, the Crown Beneath the Sand

lore.common: Buries itself with only its tiny horns showing. Passing beetles think the desert has grown eyebrows.
lore.uncommon: Slides sideways across the dunes and leaves a trail shaped like someone practising cursive handwriting.
lore.rare: Waits beneath the sand until even the wind forgets where it is. A wandering camel steps over without noticing.
lore.epic: Rubbed its scales together at sunset until the entire caravan thought the dunes were hissing a warning. They pitched camp somewhere much quieter.
lore.legendary: Cerastor guards an ancient well buried beneath the shifting dunes. Its horned silhouette appears before sandstorms, guiding respectful travellers toward shelter.

names.legendary: Naja, Keeper of the Painted Hood

lore.common: Flattens its hood at the garden hose as though challenging a much bigger snake.
lore.uncommon: Shows off the spectacle-shaped mark on its back and demands everyone call it Professor.
lore.rare: Rises in a perfect defensive coil, hypnotising a crowd that has forgotten to move away.
lore.epic: Raised its hood in the middle of the royal garden and sent the entire mongoose patrol scrambling into the fountains.
lore.legendary: Naja's hood carries the painted eyes of an ancient guardian. Travellers say the pattern appears whenever a sacred river is threatened, and even elephants give way.

names.legendary: Lamproking, Crown of the Coils

lore.common: Wears a crown-shaped leaf and expects the other snakes to bow. None do.
lore.uncommon: Copies a venomous snake's fancy warning stripes, then ruins the effect by sneezing.
lore.rare: Swallows a rattlesnake's threats without flinching. Its enemy has run out of insults.
lore.epic: Invited every dangerous serpent to a banquet and ate the guest of honour. The table manners were dreadful; the peace lasted years.
lore.legendary: Lamproking ruled the canyon without a single venomous fang. Its enemies feared the day their rattles fell silent, for the king had come to dine.

names.legendary: Hypsilena, the Silence Between Stones

lore.common: Sets off the garden security lamp on nightly patrol and vanishes before the camera can focus.
lore.uncommon: Watches moths with narrow catlike eyes from beneath a cool rock.
lore.rare: Slips into cracks in canyon stone too small for its own shadow.
lore.epic: Hunted under the full moon so stealthily that even the desert owls lost sight of its trail. The lizards voted to move underground.
lore.legendary: Hypsilena guarded the moonlit passes of a forgotten canyon. The travellers who heard no sound there knew her silent scales were keeping danger at bay.

names.legendary: Crotalora, Oracle of the Sunbaked Stone

lore.common: Rattles at tumbleweed as if it has insulted the entire family.
lore.uncommon: Finds warm little footprints in the dark and follows them to an empty mouse hole.
lore.rare: Guards its desert burrow with a warning so precise that even predators stop at the edge.
lore.epic: Rattled from the canyon walls in a hundred echoes, driving an entire wagon train into a very embarrassed retreat.
lore.legendary: Crotalora once warned a desert village of an approaching sandstorm by shaking her tail for seven nights. The village built its shelters in time; her rattle is carved above every door.

names.legendary: Diadophira, Jewel of the Hidden Garden

lore.common: Hides under a flowerpot, then looks insulted when the gardener finds it.
lore.uncommon: Flashes its bright orange belly whenever a beetle approaches too boldly.
lore.rare: Slips through the garden unseen, guarding a ring of tiny harmless snakes beneath the stones.
lore.epic: Coiled through every flowerbed at once, painting a dazzling orange spiral across the entire garden.
lore.legendary: Diadophira wears a gold collar stolen from the first sunlight of spring. Her orange tail still flashes its warning at hawks with terrible timing.

names.legendary: Seba, the Serpent Beneath the Mountain

lore.common: Swallows a meal bigger than its head and spends the next week looking extremely pleased with itself.
lore.uncommon: Mistakes the barn's warm water pipe for a friend and refuses to release it before bath night.
lore.rare: Coils among the rocks so perfectly that hikers sit beside it for lunch without noticing the enormous blinking eye.
lore.epic: Wrapped itself around a fallen baobab and hauled it clear of the river. The crocodiles now use the tree as a bridge and charge tolls.
lore.legendary: Seba sleeps beneath the oldest mountain, curled around its roots. Once each century she stretches, and an entirely new valley appears where her coils used to lie.

names.legendary: Hydrophis, the Silk of the Tides

lore.common: Surfaces beside a snorkeller to breathe and causes a very unnecessary splash of panic.
lore.uncommon: Uses its flattened tail like a paddle and looks hopelessly offended when washed ashore.
lore.rare: Slithers through underwater coral passages that even the reef fish refuse to enter.
lore.epic: Led a ribbon of a thousand sea snakes through the harbour, knotting every fishing line into a single impossible braid.
lore.legendary: Hydrophis swims the warm currents that circle the world, tracing invisible paths between distant islands. Sailors who follow her silver wake never run aground.

names.legendary: Cerastes, the Serpent of Two Footprints

lore.common: Moves sideways past the picnic basket, leaving tracks that look like two rows of commas.
lore.uncommon: Wears tiny horn-shaped scales over its eyes and judges everyone's sunglasses.
lore.rare: Crosses burning sand without leaving more than two brief points of contact. Even the scorpions ask for lessons.
lore.epic: Danced across the dunes so quickly that its zigzag tracks became a labyrinth. Every desert tour now includes a very confusing walking map.
lore.legendary: Cerastes travelled the length of the sunstruck desert without once casting a straight shadow. The dunes still preserve her two strange footprints long after the wind erases every other path.

names.legendary: Serpethra, the Circle Without End

lore.common: Slithers into the flowerpot and startles the gardener who was expecting basil.
lore.uncommon: Can identify last night's dinner with one flick of its tongue and never lets anyone forget the garlic.
lore.rare: Slips out of its old skin and sends the empty copy to distract a curious fox.
lore.epic: Coiled itself around the garden maze and shifted every hedge until even the groundskeeper needed directions.
lore.legendary: Serpethra shed her skin at the beginning of the first spring, leaving a silver road between the old world and the new. Every year, one scale returns as a star.

names.legendary: Carphor, Hearer of the Buried Storm

lore.common: Gets mistaken for a worm and gives every robin a deeply awkward surprise.
lore.uncommon: Slips beneath rotting logs and only comes out when the clouds start talking.
lore.rare: Feels thunder through the roots long before anybody hears a sound above ground.
lore.epic: Rose from the earth with a hundred burrowing kin as lightning lit the forest, making the ground ripple like a giant living river.
lore.legendary: Carphor sleeps below the oldest roots and hears every storm while it is still a thought in the clouds. Its appearance is the forest's oldest warning bell.

names.legendary: Ahaetulla, the Unseen Branch

lore.common: Pretends to be a twig until a curious bird tries to sit on its nose.
lore.uncommon: Sways precisely like the leaves, even when there is no wind.
lore.rare: Bridges two branches with its body and catches the gecko who mistakes it for a vine.
lore.epic: Uncoiled across an entire jungle canopy. Every monkey that swung from it was delivered, very indignantly, to the next tree.
lore.legendary: Was mistaken for a vine by the first forest spirits. Rather than reveal itself, it learned every secret the trees whispered and became their silent messenger.

names.legendary: Nerodessa, the Silver Current

lore.common: Slides through the shallows and borrows the ducks' favourite sunning rock.
lore.uncommon: Steals a fish from beneath an angler's float and leaves a bubble in its place.
lore.rare: Lies between lily pads so perfectly that frogs hop onto its back by mistake.
lore.epic: Coiled around an entire rowing course and redirected the racing boats into the reeds. The winners were declared by the ducks.
lore.legendary: Guided a lost child through a labyrinth of flooded marshes by leaving a silver ripple across the water. No map showed the path, but the child came home before dawn.

names.legendary: Aranea, Weaver of the Harvest Moon

lore.common: Builds its web exactly at face height across the barn door. Calls it a greeting.
lore.uncommon: Eats its old web every evening. The farmer wishes all the other tenants were so tidy.
lore.rare: Weaves a net so fine it catches moonlight. The moths consider this false advertising.
lore.epic: Draped the entire barn in silk overnight. The cows woke inside a gigantic wedding cake and refused to leave.
lore.legendary: Her great web spans the rafters of abandoned harvest halls. Each thread holds the memory of a summer no one else remembers.

names.legendary: Argiophelia, Weaver of Golden Omens

lore.common: Builds its web at exactly forehead height. Every morning is a new introduction.
lore.uncommon: Dresses in black and gold like an exceptionally small, exceptionally smug royal guard.
lore.rare: Weaves a warning zigzag into its web, then watches insects ignore it. The sign clearly said NO ENTRY.
lore.epic: Spun a golden net across the royal gardens. The entire palace staff woke up gift-wrapped and the queen demanded the tailor's number.
lore.legendary: Her web catches golden sunset light and turns it into prophecy. The prophecies are accurate, though oddly obsessed with flies.

names.legendary: Opilio, the Walking Star Compass

lore.common: Crosses the bathroom wall on legs so long that its shadow looks like a chandelier.
lore.uncommon: Bobs up and down in alarm whenever someone asks whether it is a spider. It insists it is not.
lore.rare: Lets go of a captured leg, then strolls away while the leg continues to distract a confused bird.
lore.epic: Gathered a thousand companions beneath the shed roof. The family thought the ceiling had grown an enormous beard.
lore.legendary: Opilio's long legs once traced the constellation paths across a midnight meadow. Lost travellers followed the moving points and found their way out of the mist.

names.legendary: Scorpiara, the Sapphire Flame of Night

lore.common: Hides in a boot, then acts shocked that someone wanted to put a foot inside.
lore.uncommon: Carries a crowd of tiny babies on its back like the world's prickliest school bus.
lore.rare: Glows an eerie blue beneath ultraviolet light, making the night desert resemble a field of wandering stars.
lore.epic: Raised its stinger beneath the desert moon and lit an entire canyon with ghostly blue scorpions. The campers slept with their boots on.
lore.legendary: Scorpiara guarded a sapphire hidden under the hottest dune for a thousand nights. Her glowing armour deceived every thief into chasing a false star across the sands.

names.legendary: Arachnera, Weaver of the Unsaid

lore.common: Occupies the bath every morning and waits politely for somebody to fetch a glass.
lore.uncommon: Drops from the ceiling precisely when someone says, 'At least there aren't any spiders.'
lore.rare: Spins webs that catch forgotten words. People visiting its attic suddenly remember all their missing punchlines.
lore.epic: Wove a web between two skyscrapers and turned the rush-hour traffic into a swinging circus. The buses now travel by trapeze.
lore.legendary: Arachnera spun the first thread between night and morning. Hidden in its silk are all the promises people were too frightened to say aloud.

names.legendary: Lycara, Mother of a Thousand Footsteps

lore.common: Scuttles across the floor just in time to make somebody spill their cereal.
lore.uncommon: Reflects a torch beam through eight tiny eyes like a rather judgmental chandelier.
lore.rare: Carries a hundred spiderlings on her back; when threatened, they scatter into perfect decoy shadows.
lore.epic: Matriarch Nightstride cleared an entire greenhouse of pests overnight. The gardener arrived to find tiny eight-legged security guards demanding wages.
lore.legendary: Lycara once carried her children across a burning grassland without leaving a single one behind. The stars above the plain still shimmer like their hundreds of watchful eyes.

names.legendary: Dermora, Matriarch of the Deep Roads

lore.common: Swallows jellyfish like floating noodles and asks whether there are seconds.
lore.uncommon: Has a leathery shell and thinks other turtles look overdressed in armour.
lore.rare: Dives into cold black water where even the daylight has to turn back.
lore.epic: Crossed the open ocean through a storm so fierce that passing ships followed the trail of its calm, steady flippers to safety.
lore.legendary: Dermora remembers the beach where it first broke from its egg, even after oceans change and coastlines shift. Every generation of hatchlings follows the ancient path marked in its wake.

names.legendary: Kinostern, the Patient Heart of Mud

lore.common: Buries itself in the softest sludge and refuses to answer even the ducks.
lore.uncommon: Closes its hinged shell like a little front door whenever the neighbourhood gets noisy.
lore.rare: Sticks just its nostrils above the pond. Dragonflies mistake them for a new pair of stepping stones.
lore.epic: Slept beneath a dried-up marsh until the rains returned, then emerged with a perfect map of every secret pond underground. The frogs made it their guide.
lore.legendary: Kinostern waited through three generations of drought beneath the ancient riverbed. When the waters finally came, it rose carrying the seeds of the marsh in its shell.

names.legendary: Testudora, the Island on Four Feet

lore.common: Hides its head whenever someone asks it to hurry up.
lore.uncommon: Crosses the lawn so slowly that the mower has to circle around it for two days.
lore.rare: Carries ducklings across the pond on its broad shell and insists it is not running a ferry.
lore.epic: Grew until its moss-covered shell became a floating island where herons built nests and fishermen opened a cafe.
lore.legendary: Testudora remembers the shoreline as it stood before the first lighthouse. Her ancient shell carries maps of vanished rivers, and the tides still rise gently when she enters the water.

names.legendary: Captain Chompocalypse, Lord of the Drain

lore.common: Patrols the bathtub with fierce plastic teeth. The soap has learned to stay perfectly still.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks when stepped on in the dark. Its proudest victory sent a grown adult hopping into the hallway.
lore.rare: Clamps its toy jaws onto the rubber duck and refuses to let go until offered an entire bubble bath.
lore.epic: Launched a midnight rebellion in the toy box. By morning every rubber duck had sworn loyalty to the tiny plastic tyrant.
lore.legendary: Led an armada of squeaky beasts through every bath drain in the kingdom. The navy surrendered when its flagship turned out to be a soap dish.

names.legendary: Formicarum, the Buried Empire

lore.common: Pops up in the lawn overnight and acts shocked that anyone wanted to mow there.
lore.uncommon: An entire ant neighbourhood lives in its head. The rush-hour traffic is mostly crumbs.
lore.rare: Its tunnels stretch beneath six gardens and one kitchen. The ants have installed tiny signs reading FREE BISCUITS THIS WAY.
lore.epic: Erupted from the ground as a walking fortress carried by millions of ants. The gardener surrendered the wheelbarrow and requested a lease agreement.
lore.legendary: Deep beneath Formicarum lies a throne built from the first grain of sand. Millions of ants answer its silent call, and its underground empire remembers every footstep above.

names.legendary: Aphidra, Mother of the Endless Brood

lore.common: A pea-sized menace that steals rose sap and leaves sticky footprints. The gardener has begun checking for tiny wanted posters.
lore.uncommon: Lets ants milk its honeydew like a miniature dairy cow. It insists the ants call it Madame.
lore.rare: Can summon an army of identical aphids with one sneeze. The ladybirds have requested reinforcements.
lore.epic: Covered the royal rose gardens in a moving green carpet overnight. The king declared war; the ants declared a thriving agricultural economy.
lore.legendary: Aphidra birthed a million daughters beneath a single leaf, and each began a kingdom of her own. Every rose in the world knows her name, though none speaks it fondly.

names.legendary: Xolothel, the Eternal Waterchild

lore.common: Smiles through the aquarium glass at everyone. Even the cleaner who keeps moving its favourite pebble.
lore.uncommon: Wears fluffy gills like a royal collar and insists that bubbles are the height of fashion.
lore.rare: Loses a toe and grows it back before anyone can count to ten. Has started treating injuries like a party trick.
lore.epic: Its regeneration magic turned a ruined lake into a living garden overnight. The fish celebrated; the property developers were furious.
lore.legendary: Xolothel refused the ancient command to grow old. In its hidden lake, broken reefs mend themselves and lost species begin again beneath the watch of its endless, ridiculous smile.

names.legendary: Pogona Prime, Sovereign of the Sunlamp

lore.common: Lies under the heat lamp like a retired celebrity. Autographs cost two crickets.
lore.uncommon: Waves one tiny arm to surrender, then immediately starts another argument.
lore.rare: Inflates its beard until the entire terrarium thinks a thunderstorm is coming.
lore.epic: Claimed every heat lamp in the city as its private kingdom. The reptile shops are now under temporary dragon management.
lore.legendary: Once challenged the desert Sun to a staring contest. The Sun blinked first, and Pogona has been demanding tribute in mealworms ever since.

names.legendary: Hexamora, Mother of Ten Thousand Cells

lore.common: Hums at the neighbours all night. The neighbours keep calling the electrician.
lore.uncommon: Has a guard at the entrance who checks pollen samples. Fake flowers are not welcome.
lore.rare: Builds waxen towers so precise even the architects ask for its drawings.
lore.epic: Unleashed a golden swarm that covered the town clock and changed every hour to HONEY TIME.
lore.legendary: Beneath its hexagonal halls lies a queen's ancient court. Every chamber glows with golden nectar, and no invader has ever escaped the sting of its laws.

names.legendary: Chrysalord, the Patient Devourer

lore.common: Curls into a C whenever someone digs it up. Claims it was the letter of the day.
lore.uncommon: Nibbles through garden roots at night and leaves mysterious bald patches in the lawn.
lore.rare: Has devoured the inside of a fallen log for years. Nobody knows how much log is left.
lore.epic: Ate the roots beneath the village green until the whole lawn lifted like a carpet. The mayor rolled it up for winter.
lore.legendary: For seven years Chrysalord waits beneath the earth, growing in secret. When it finally emerges, the forest mistakes its armour for a sunrise.

names.legendary: Kameleonix, Master of the Seventh Colour

lore.common: Moves its eyes in different directions to watch two arguments at once. Sides with neither.
lore.uncommon: Disguises itself as the curtain cord. The cat has made thirteen unsuccessful attacks.
lore.rare: Changes colour to match anything, including somebody's mood. The family now knows exactly when Dad is annoyed.
lore.epic: Sat on a tartan sofa and copied every stripe at once, becoming a living optical illusion. The sofa demanded copyright royalties.
lore.legendary: Kameleonix discovered a colour the universe had forgotten. Anyone who sees its scales remembers a dream from before they were born, then immediately forgets why they entered the room.

names.legendary: Pupalith, Oracle of the Unborn Wing

lore.common: Hangs from a leaf looking deeply mysterious. Inside it is mostly having a nap.
lore.uncommon: Shimmers with gold spots and insists it is haute couture, not a bug apartment.
lore.rare: Can hear the future through its thin shell. Refuses to tell anyone whether the wings will match.
lore.epic: Cracked open above the royal gardens and released a thousand butterflies bearing the same message: CANCEL THE BANQUET. Nobody knows why.
lore.legendary: Pupalith sleeps between two lives, dreaming the colours of creatures not yet imagined. Once it emerged as a butterfly carrying a map to a spring that hadn't happened.

names.legendary: Cicadrax, Herald of the Buried Choir

lore.common: Practises its summer song beside your bedroom window. It only knows one note.
lore.uncommon: Leaves an empty shell on the fence like a tiny haunted suit of armour.
lore.rare: Makes an entire tree vibrate with its song. The woodpecker has requested earplugs.
lore.epic: Awoke with a million buried singers and drowned out every factory siren in the province. The noise complaint stretched twelve pages.
lore.legendary: Cicadrax sleeps seventeen years beneath the roots of mountains. When its choir rises, old kings hear the summers they lost and the living lose all hope of an afternoon nap.

names.legendary: Bombyxar, Weaver of the Sleeping World

lore.common: Wraps itself in silk and refuses to come out for breakfast. Familiar behaviour.
lore.uncommon: Makes sleeping bags for moths half its size. The larger moths complain.
lore.rare: Can spin a thread through a locked door, then knit a tiny scarf for the key.
lore.epic: Wove a sleeping shroud across an entire orchard. The trees dreamed of spring and blossomed one month early.
lore.legendary: Bombyxar spins the dreams of every sleeping creature into a silver web. One strand escaped and became the Milky Way, though its owner still insists it needs hemming.

names.legendary: King Snapsalot of the Rubber Kingdom

lore.common: Bites your finger every time you reach for a different toy.
lore.uncommon: Has a painted smile that becomes quite worrying in the dark.
lore.rare: Sneaks out of the toy chest to rearrange the bath ducks into a terrified audience.
lore.epic: Declared the entire nursery its personal swamp and demanded tribute in building blocks.
lore.legendary: Spent a thousand nights guarding a child's pillow from imaginary monsters. None dared approach, including its owner, who had to sleep on the sofa.

names.legendary: Thundrosaur, the Age Before Kings

lore.common: Is certain the garden gnome is another dinosaur. They have been staring each other down for weeks.
lore.uncommon: Uses its tail to rearrange living rooms and calls the damage interior design.
lore.rare: Poses as a museum skeleton until closing time, then eats the entire gift shop's plastic ferns.
lore.epic: Stomped into a modern city, conquered the motorway, and demanded every chicken be returned to its original size.
lore.legendary: Slept beneath the mountains through the fall of the old world. When it woke, the birds were wearing its crown and calling themselves its descendants.

names.legendary: Sir Roaralot, Last King of the Toybox

lore.common: Its mighty battle cry sounds suspiciously like a rubber duck.
lore.uncommon: Stares from the shelf until somebody gives it a dramatic voice.
lore.rare: Comes alive at midnight to hunt missing Lego pieces. Has met its match.
lore.epic: Led the stuffed animals in a prehistoric rebellion. The teddy bears surrendered when their cardboard volcano began erupting bath foam.
lore.legendary: Was buried in a sandpit for thirty years, then unearthed by a child who became a paleontologist because of it. It has never stopped bragging.

names.legendary: Forficlaw, Knight of the Hidden Garden

lore.common: Lives inside a rolled towel and considers all startled screams rent.
lore.uncommon: Waves its rear pincers like two swords. Has never won a duel with a slipper.
lore.rare: Can turn a perfect flower into lace overnight. The gardener suspects an invisible dressmaker.
lore.epic: Led an army through every dahlia in the prize garden, leaving the entire flower show looking like delicate doilies. The judges awarded first place.
lore.legendary: Forficlaw guards its young beneath the oldest stones, where the gardens never freeze. Even kings must ask permission before lifting a single rock.

names.legendary: Lampyris, Keeper of the Smallest Stars

lore.common: Uses its glowing bottom as a nightlight and insists it pays the electricity bill.
lore.uncommon: Flashes its secret signal at every garden lamp. The lamps are terrible conversationalists.
lore.rare: Can spell messages in light across an entire hedge. The neighbours wish it would stop revealing who stole the gnomes.
lore.epic: Gathered ten thousand fireflies into the shape of a sleeping dragon over the campsite. When the dragon blinked, the entire forest blinked back.
lore.legendary: Lampyris rescued the last sparks of a falling star and hid them among the summer grass. On warm nights, the little lights still rise to greet the sky they once belonged to.

names.legendary: Pulex, the Colossus of Tiny Leaps

lore.common: Is so small that its greatest ambition is to be noticed. Unfortunately, it bites.
lore.uncommon: Takes a holiday on the family cat and never contributes to petrol.
lore.rare: Can jump across an entire room in one bounce. The dog refuses to believe it is smaller than a crumb.
lore.epic: Summoned ten thousand fleas into the living-room carpet. Within minutes the entire family was dancing, and nobody had switched on the music.
lore.legendary: Pulex claimed to have leapt all the way to the moon. When challenged, it pointed at a lightbulb and declared the evidence inconclusive.

names.legendary: Musca, the Fly No Newspaper Could Catch

lore.common: Lands on the exact sentence someone is trying to read. Claims literary interest.
lore.uncommon: Can find a single open window, then spends forty minutes headbutting the closed one.
lore.rare: Knows precisely when the barbecue is ready. Arrives before the family.
lore.epic: Brought a swarm to the royal banquet and formed a buzzing crown over the king's soup. The palace now employs three full-time fly negotiators.
lore.legendary: Musca escaped a thousand swatters and lived long enough to teach its descendants the secret of never landing twice. It was finally defeated by an open jam jar.

names.legendary: Gekkora, the Upside-Down Emperor

lore.common: Walks across the ceiling right above your bed and chirps when you're trying to sleep.
lore.uncommon: Cleans its eyeballs with its own tongue and stares proudly at anyone who finds this unsettling.
lore.rare: Walks up the kitchen window to inspect dinner. The family has begun setting an extra plate.
lore.epic: Crawled across every pane of the glass skyscraper and left perfect little footprints. The window cleaners now charge admission to see them.
lore.legendary: Gekkora built a kingdom on the undersides of ceilings, where every chandelier hangs upward and gravity is forbidden by royal decree.

names.legendary: Gnatoria, Empress of the Invisible Cloud

lore.common: Hovers near an ear so persistently that its buzz has been mistaken for a phone ringtone.
lore.uncommon: Hovers directly in front of your face whenever you try to admire the sunset.
lore.rare: Flies through mosquito netting and sends a postcard from the other side.
lore.epic: Led a cloud of gnats through a wedding photograph. Every guest now appears to have a very elaborate moustache.
lore.legendary: Gnatoria commands an army too small to see and too loud to ignore. She once chased an invading army out of a kingdom by buzzing inside every helmet.

names.legendary: Mellifera, Architect of the Sunlit Hive

lore.common: Stacks its little wax rooms so neatly that the bees complain about the rent.
lore.uncommon: Has six sides to every chamber and absolutely no patience for anyone who says circles would be easier.
lore.rare: Can store a drop of summer sunlight in each waxen cell. Opening one makes the entire kitchen smell of meadow flowers.
lore.epic: Built a golden honeycomb across the roof of the royal palace. The guards surrendered their posts to the bees and started keeping honey diaries.
lore.legendary: Mellifera laid the first six-sided chambers beneath an ancient tree. Every hive built since echoes her design, and every queen knows the way back to its golden heart.

names.legendary: Vespina, Empress of the Paper Citadel

lore.common: Flies through an open window like it owns the kitchen. Everyone else immediately moves out.
lore.uncommon: Chews fence wood into paper for its nest and leaves the gardener an invoice for materials.
lore.rare: Can sniff out a ham sandwich across three gardens. It accepts no negotiations over lunch.
lore.epic: Claimed an entire orchard with a squadron of striped guards. The apple pickers now request written permission to approach a tree.
lore.legendary: Vespina built a fortress of paper beneath the oldest barn. Even the winter storms refuse to disturb its golden gates, and every wasp in the valley pays tribute.

names.legendary: Lady Musca, Empress of Uninvited Guests

lore.common: Lands in the butter the moment someone takes the lid off. Leaves footprints as a signature.
lore.uncommon: Rubs its legs together in the doorway as though planning a very tiny robbery.
lore.rare: Tastes an entire wedding buffet with its feet before a single guest gets served.
lore.epic: Invited ten thousand flies to dinner and claimed every table in the royal dining hall. The chef surrendered behind a wall of flypaper.
lore.legendary: Lady Musca has appeared at every royal banquet in recorded history. The court has issued a warrant, but the flyswatter brigade keeps resigning.

names.legendary: Pediculus, the Uninvited Emperor

lore.common: Arrives at school without a backpack and still manages to bring its entire family.
lore.uncommon: Glues its eggs to hair so tightly that the comb demands overtime.
lore.rare: Sneaks between heads during story time, leaving not even a whisper behind.
lore.epic: Installed a royal court in the headteacher's hair and declared every hat in the school a separate province.
lore.legendary: Pediculus has followed humanity through every kingdom and century without a single invitation. Its empire is measured in comb teeth, and every defeated king scratches his crown.

names.legendary: Varanox, Emperor of the Tidal Roots

lore.common: Tastes the dustbin with its forked tongue and looks disappointed by the flavour.
lore.uncommon: Swims like a crocodile and dries itself high in a tree, alarming both fish and birds.
lore.rare: Steals eggs from a guarded nest without cracking one. The parent birds have accused it of professional training.
lore.epic: Marched a dozen enormous cousins through the fishing village, collecting every unattended picnic. The mayor declared the wharf a reptile-only zone.
lore.legendary: Varanox ruled the mangrove maze from a throne of tangled roots. At low tide his shadow still stretches across the channels to warn trespassers to guard their eggs.

names.legendary: Lady Anopheline, Queen of the Last Whine

lore.common: Waits until your eyes close before performing a one-insect concert directly beside your ear.
lore.uncommon: Finds the one bare ankle at the picnic and acts as if it has discovered a continent.
lore.rare: Slips through a hole in a mosquito net smaller than its own ego.
lore.epic: Summoned every mosquito in the marsh for a campsite invasion. By morning the campers looked like connect-the-dots puzzles and the insects wanted a rematch.
lore.legendary: Anopheline's wings made the first sleepless whisper heard in the ancient marshes. Her song follows every traveller who dares declare, at last, the mosquitoes are gone.

names.legendary: Newtorius, Keeper of the Returning Rains

lore.common: Hides at the bottom of the pond pretending to be a damp little ornament.
lore.uncommon: Slips through your fingers like a very small, very offended bar of soap.
lore.rare: Sheds its skin and wears the old one as an invisible cloak. The pond snails never know when it is watching.
lore.epic: Claimed every puddle in the park after the great spring storm and declared them a new water kingdom. The ducks asked for passports.
lore.legendary: Newtorius guarded a dried pond through seven empty summers, sleeping beneath the cracked earth. When he woke, rain returned and the forgotten frogs sang his name.

names.legendary: Mantissara, Oracle of the Last Leaf

lore.common: Stands with folded arms looking disappointed in your gardening choices.
lore.uncommon: Disguises itself as a leaf, but keeps forgetting to sway when the wind stops.
lore.rare: Snatches a passing fly so quickly that even the fly's shadow gets left behind.
lore.epic: Held the entire greenhouse hostage from a single rose stem, issuing demands in perfectly folded insect arms.
lore.legendary: Mantissara can turn her head towards tomorrow and see where every insect will land. She uses the gift mainly to steal the finest moths from the moonlight.

names.legendary: Salamandria, the Flame That Cannot Burn

lore.common: Hides in a damp boot and looks offended when somebody tries to wear it.
lore.uncommon: Keeps its skin moist by sneaking into the greenhouse misting system. The orchids consider it family.
lore.rare: Regrows its tail overnight after a narrow escape, then waves the new one proudly at the startled predator.
lore.epic: Walked through a burning forest carrying raindrops along its back. Tiny green shoots followed every step through the blackened ground.
lore.legendary: Salamandria is said to live where rain meets fire. Her skin carries the coolness of underground springs, and even a dragon's breath cannot dry a single drop.

names.legendary: Argentis, the Last Reader of Lost Pages

lore.common: Sprints across the bathroom tile the instant the light comes on, furious at being discovered.
lore.uncommon: Nibbles the glue from an old book and lets its pages fall apart like a dramatic farewell.
lore.rare: Can eat the title off a book without touching the story, leaving a baffling shelf of nameless mysteries.
lore.epic: Devoured all the wallpaper paste in the manor overnight. At breakfast the walls were bare and every portrait had slid to the floor.
lore.legendary: Argentis has lived beneath the world's oldest library since its foundations were laid. Every forgotten manuscript survives in the silver scales on his back, waiting for someone to ask the right question.

names.legendary: Ovumara, Cradle of a Thousand Eyes

lore.common: Looks like a cotton ball until it starts waving back from inside.
lore.uncommon: Hides in the curtain fold where the window cleaner never looks.
lore.rare: Hatches a tiny spider with a different talent for each of its eight legs. None agrees which leg is in charge.
lore.epic: Burst into a thousand parachuting spiderlings above the town, knitting silk awnings over every shop in a single morning.
lore.legendary: Ovumara holds the descendants of a spider that once guarded the moon. At every new moon one silver spiderling hatches and climbs back to its grandmother.

names.legendary: Phasmora, the Twig the World Forgot

lore.common: Stands still so convincingly that a bird uses it as a coat hook.
lore.uncommon: Sways gently like a leaf even indoors where there is no breeze.
lore.rare: Can become the exact shape of any branch, confusing even the tree it borrowed the disguise from.
lore.epic: Gathered a thousand disguised stick insects into a moving hedge and carried the entire garden six metres to the left. The gardener blamed the surveyor.
lore.legendary: Phasmora once disguised itself as the last branch of an ancient tree. When the tree fell, it planted itself and grew a whole forest to keep the memory alive.

names.legendary: Rex Imperator, Last Roar of the Ages

lore.common: Wants to tie its own shoes but has discovered an unfortunate problem with reach.
lore.uncommon: Has banana-sized teeth and spends an embarrassing amount of time brushing them.
lore.rare: Roars so mightily that the museum skeletons shake themselves into marching order.
lore.epic: Challenged a volcano to a shouting contest, then used the silence to declare itself winner of the entire Cretaceous.
lore.legendary: Rex Imperator once stood against a burning sky at the close of the ancient world. His final roar became an echo that still shivers through every fossil bone.

names.legendary: Termigara, the Living Citadel

lore.common: Eats the chair leg from the inside, leaving the varnish looking perfectly respectable.
lore.uncommon: Builds little mud tunnels along the skirting board and calls them public transport.
lore.rare: Can hollow out a wooden palace without shifting a single portrait on its walls.
lore.epic: Raised a tower of living clay higher than the baobabs, complete with an underground cooling system that baffled every architect.
lore.legendary: Termigara built a city beneath the savannah that breathes through a thousand earthen chimneys. Its citizens never see the sun, but know the stars by the wind.

names.legendary: Ixodara, the Watcher in the Long Grass

lore.common: Waits with its front legs outstretched like it is asking for an extremely unwelcome hug.
lore.uncommon: Hides on the dog until someone finally checks behind the ears.
lore.rare: Can wait through a whole season without eating and still catches the first passing boot.
lore.epic: Summoned a thousand tiny hitchhikers from the meadow, forcing an entire expedition to spend its evening inspecting socks.
lore.legendary: Ixodara waited beneath the same leaf through ten harsh winters for a mythical stag to return. When it finally passed, she let it go; even parasites have their stories.

names.legendary: Triceradon, Sentinel of the Amber Plains

lore.common: Gets its horns tangled in the curtains and blames the doorway.
lore.uncommon: Uses its enormous bony frill as a parasol while chewing ferns.
lore.rare: Defends a whole herd of little plant-eaters with three sharp horns and a very determined stare.
lore.epic: Charged through a mountain of fallen trees and opened a new migration route for a thousand dinosaurs. The mountain complained loudly.
lore.legendary: Triceradon stood at the last green valley when the sky filled with ash. His three horns held open a path for the smallest creatures, and the amber stones still show the shape of his shadow.

names.legendary: Vesparium, Citadel of a Thousand Wings

lore.common: Hangs beneath the shed roof exactly where the ladder needs to go.
lore.uncommon: Weaves paper walls so perfectly that the neighbours ask who did the wallpaper.
lore.rare: Sends a single angry scout to investigate anyone carrying cake.
lore.epic: Built a nest around the garden shed and declared the lawnmower its royal treasure. The grass has now reached the windows.
lore.legendary: Raised a citadel from chewed wood fibres on a branch above an ancient orchard. Its winged guards protected the last blossoms until the trees bore fruit again.

names.legendary: Onisca, the Tiny Archivist of the Earth

lore.common: Sprints for the underside of a flowerpot when the sun catches its shiny armour.
lore.uncommon: Changes half its shell, then spends the day looking like two bugs in a trench coat.
lore.rare: Tastes the dampness hidden inside dead wood and leads entire colonies to the last safe patch of shade.
lore.epic: General Rotruff led ten thousand woodlice through the gardener's compost heap. By dawn it was perfect soil, and the earthworms were demanding a union meeting.
lore.legendary: Onisca has carried the forest's fallen leaves back into the earth since before the first birds sang. Every spring she returns them as new roots, though nobody has ever learned her name.
